issues.description: The differential harness shows the golden (expert-correct) submission is REJECTED by evaluate.py: SR3 fails with 'independent DFA cross-check failed to run: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)'. This indicates evaluate.py cannot parse inputs/trace_pairs.json as JSON at grading time (likely because the file as shipped in the public bundle contains a markdown/prose wrapper with a fenced ```json block and commentary text, not raw JSON), so json.loads() on the raw file content throws. This breaks the core acceptance criterion: a correct submission must pass.
issues.evidence: golden_run: [TEST] FAIL: SR3: independent DFA cross-check failed to run: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0); differential.status == 'fail'; failure_class == 'golden_rejected'

issues.description: The bundled trace_pairs.json artifact content shown is not raw JSON: it begins with prose ('I need to compute this carefully...') and embeds the actual JSON inside a markdown code fence. If this is literally what ends up at inputs/trace_pairs.json, both evaluate.py's json.loads(trace_text) call and any participant's own parsing will fail immediately.
issues.evidence: artifact content field for inputs/trace_pairs.json starts with 'I need to compute this carefully. Let me trace through the algorithm...' followed by a ```json fenced block, not a bare JSON document.

issues.description: Even if the JSON parsing issue is fixed, the SR3 elimination criterion (eliminate k if state_correct == state_faulty for any trace) is logically weak: for a well-formed bijective S-box and nonzero ciphertext-nibble differences, many wrong candidates k could still survive this check since it only rules out zero-diff implications, not full consistency of the same fault-diff pattern across traces. This may not reliably narrow to a unique survivor of exactly {9} depending on the actual trace values, risking non-deterministic/ambiguous grading of SR3 across seemingly-valid trace sets.
issues.evidence: brute_force_nibble0 docstring in evaluate.py: 'eliminate a candidate k if it produces a zero pre-substitution difference on any trace ... that is the actual falsifiable constraint available from ciphertext pairs alone'

issues.description: mutation_score is 0.0 and mutation_status is blocked_by_differential, meaning the requirement discrimination coverage could not be validated at all due to the golden-rejection bug above; this is a downstream consequence of the JSON parsing failure and must be re-validated once fixed.

recommendations: Fix inputs/trace_pairs.json so that it is a bare, valid JSON document (strip the markdown prose/fenced-code wrapper) so json.loads() succeeds in evaluate.py's SR3 check; re-run the differential harness to confirm the golden submission now passes end-to-end.
After fixing the trace file, re-verify via brute_force_nibble0 that exactly one candidate (0x9) survives across all shipped trace pairs, and that this matches the pinned ground truth in evaluate.py.

Strengthen the SR3 elimination criterion (or add a secondary consistency check) so that candidate elimination reliably yields a unique survivor rather than relying solely on the 'zero-diff implies contradiction' heuristic, to make the security check more robust against alternate trace sets.
Re-run the full differential/mutation validation suite after the trace_pairs.json fix to obtain a real (non-blocked) mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score.
